description: Implement the legora scan command: repository inventory collection via git ls-files, knowledge coverage mapping (covered/stale/uncovered), module-level grouping, CLI integration with --depth and --json flags, human-readable and JSON output, and comprehensive unit tests.
steps: Create src/scan/contracts.ts defining types: CoverageStatus ('covered'|'stale'|'uncovered'), FileInventoryEntry ({filePath, coverageStatus}), ModuleSummary ({module, total, covered, stale, uncovered, files}), ScanResult ({totalFiles, coveredFiles, staleFiles, uncoveredFiles, modules, files, depth})

Create src/scan/inventory.ts with function collectRepositoryInventory(repositoryRoot): uses child_process.execFile to run `git ls-files` (tracked files only). Filters out common non-source patterns (.git/, node_modules/, etc). Returns string[] of relative file paths.

Create src/scan/coverage.ts with function computeScanCoverage(repositoryRoot, options?:{depth:'file'|'module'}): 1) calls collectRepositoryInventory to get file list, 2) calls readKnowledgeRecords to load knowledge, 3) for each file checks if any record's activeEvidence[].filePath references it, 4) for referenced files calls checkKnowledgeRecordFreshness on the relevant records to determine CURRENT->covered, STALE->stale, UNKNOWN->stale (fail-closed), 5) files with no evidence reference are uncovered, 6) groups results by directory (module), 7) returns ScanResult.
Add renderScanResult(result: ScanResult): string function to src/cli/render.ts that produces human-readable text output with summary stats and per-module breakdown.

Add 'scan' command dispatch to src/cli/index.ts in runCliCommand(): parse --depth (file|module, default module) and --json flags, call computeScanCoverage, return CliCommandResult with stdout (human-readable) or data (JSON mode).
Add USAGE entry for 'legora scan [--depth file|module] [--json]' to the USAGE constant in src/cli/index.ts.
Create tests/unit/scan/inventory.test.ts: test collectRepositoryInventory with a temp git repo (git init + git add + git commit), verify it returns tracked files and excludes untracked files.

Create tests/unit/scan/coverage.test.ts: test computeScanCoverage with mock git repos containing knowledge records. Test scenarios: (a) file covered by CURRENT knowledge -> 'covered', (b) file covered by STALE knowledge -> 'stale', (c) file with no knowledge reference -> 'uncovered', (d) module grouping aggregates correctly, (e) empty repo (no knowledge) -> all uncovered.

Create tests/unit/scan/scan-cli.test.ts: test the scan CLI command via runCliCommand(['scan'], repoRoot) in both default and --json modes. Verify exit code 0, correct data structure, and human-readable stdout presence.
acceptance_criteria: Running `npm run typecheck` passes with zero errors including the new scan module
Running `npm test` passes all tests including new tests/unit/scan/*.test.ts files
`legora scan` on a repo with knowledge records correctly classifies files as covered/stale/uncovered
`legora scan --json` outputs structured JSON with totalFiles, coveredFiles, staleFiles, uncoveredFiles, modules, files
`legora scan --depth file` shows per-file detail; `--depth module` (default) shows module grouping
Files referenced by knowledge records with CURRENT freshness are 'covered'
Files referenced by knowledge records with STALE or UNKNOWN freshness are 'stale' (fail-closed)
Files not referenced by any knowledge record evidence are 'uncovered'
Inventory is collected via git ls-files (tracked files only, inherently respects .gitignore)
